newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa down on Azcarraga news-traders.
newsitem.headline: Televisa down on Azcarraga news-traders.

text.p: Shares of Grupo Televisa SA were sharply lower in mid-afternoon trade on news the media group's chairman Emilio Azcarraga Milmo -- known as "The Tiger" -- has taken leave for medical care in Los Angeles, traders said.
The company said Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer Emilio Azcarraga Jean, Azcarraga Milmo's son, will be responsible for broadcasting operations in the absence of Azcarraga Milmo.
Televisa's CPO shares were off five pesos at 102.00 pesos, while its ADRs had fallen 1-1/8 to 26-1/4 on Wall Street.
The company did not detail what health trouble Azcarraga faced, but traders speculated it was heart trouble.
"Share prices began to fall this morning on rumors Azcarraga had had a heart attack and maybe dealers did not like the company being left in his son's hands," a desk trader said.

"It's more than just profit-taking. The stock began to fall when a rumor arose this morning that Azcarraga had had a heart attack. The underlying concern is what will happen to a one-man company after he is gone," another desk trader said.
Business columnist Alberto Aguilar wrote in the local daily Reforma on Thursday "It also transpired yesterday that Emilio Azcarraga Milmo is in a delicate state of health."
Aguila added that Azcarraga, aged 66, recently missed a Televisa board meeting for the first time.
